effects.target: Answers to four questions about the creature whose blood you touch - the name it is known by, its gender/race/profession, how its blood was shed, and when - appear written on any flat surface you designate, in a language you can read. A living or undead source is entitled to a Will save to refuse.

blood-biography.notes: Pure divination; nothing in the vocabulary expresses 'answers appear written on a surface'.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: fatigued
on_failure.note: round 1 of 3, on the round the spell is cast

effects.target: Round 2 (new Fortitude save at the start of your turn): capillaries burst for 1d6 points of Constitution damage. Round 3 (new save again): the blood boils for 1d6 points of damage per caster level, maximum 15d6, and a target still alive becomes exhausted rather than fatigued. A successful save prevents only that round's effect and does not end the spell.

blood-boil.notes: Staged over three rounds with a fresh save each round. Only round 1 (fatigued) happens at cast time, so only that round is executable; rounds 2 and 3 are named exactly in the narrative spec because the vocabulary has no way to schedule an effect for a later round. Deliberately did not emit the 1d6/level damage as a damage spec - it would fire immediately instead of on round 3.

effects.target: Make unarmed strike or flurry of blows attacks against one creature within medium range as if it were in your threatened area; each hit deals your normal unarmed strike damage, half of it fire and half negative energy, and that negative energy does not heal undead.

blood-crow-strike.notes: The '2d6' in the prose is a worked example for a 14th-level monk, not the spell's damage - not converted. The damage is the unarmed strike's, not the spell's. Element already derived as fire from the descriptor.

effects.target: str
effects.note: only sharks, feeders in the depths, and creatures with the blood frenzy ability, and only while inside the emanation

effects.target: con
effects.note: only sharks, feeders in the depths, and creatures with the blood frenzy ability, and only while inside the emanation

effects.target: ac
effects.note: same creatures as the Strength and Constitution bonuses

effects.target: As part of casting you deal yourself 1 point of piercing or slashing damage, which puts you at 1 point of bleed. The spell ends immediately if you stop bleeding. The bonuses count as blood frenzy for other feats and effects and do not stack with real blood frenzy.

blood-in-the-water.notes: Bonuses are untyped - the prose names no bonus type. The 1 point of bleed is taken by the CASTER while the bonuses go to creatures in the emanation, and no spec has a recipient field, so the self-cost is narrated rather than emitted as a bleed spec that would land on the wrong creatures.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: wis
on_failure.note: one save per entry into the mist; leaving and returning forces a new save

effects.target: A 60-foot radius of rust-red toxic algae. Every creature inside is stained red and gains concealment. A creature that fails its save is also enraged for as long as the spell lasts, always taking the 'attack nearest creature' result of the confused condition rather than rolling on the confusion table.

blood-mist.notes: Did not emit apply_condition confused: the prose pins the behaviour to one fixed result ('attack nearest creature'), and applying real confusion would make the engine roll randomly instead. Concealment has no condition in the vocabulary.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target bleeds for 1d6 points of bleed damage per 4 caster levels, to a maximum of 4d6 at 16th level, taken when the spell is cast. The bleed continues after the spell ends until stopped by magical healing or a DC 15 Heal check.

effects.target: A creature that spends a full-round action supping the willing or helpless subject's blood heals twice the hit points the subject lost to the bleed that round; only one creature per round can be healed this way, and doing so provokes attacks of opportunity. The subject may lick her own wounds instead to regain half as many hit points as she lost that round.

blood-of-the-martyr.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: bleed takes an integer amount only, so '1d6 bleed per 4 caster levels' cannot be expressed as a bleed spec - narrated with the exact numbers instead of rounding to an integer. The healing goes to a THIRD PARTY who drinks the blood, not to the spell's target, so it is not emitted as a heal spec. No scaling block: the progression is on bleed, not on damage dice.

effects.target: For every 5 points of damage an affected creature takes, it gains a cumulative +2 morale bonus to Strength and a cumulative -1 penalty to AC, to a maximum of +10 Strength and -5 AC. These last until the spell expires or the target falls unconscious.

blood-rage.notes: Did not emit ability_mod +2 morale Strength: the bonus is not granted on casting, it accrues per 5 damage taken. A flat +2 at cast time would be wrong in both direction and magnitude.

effects.target: damage from your own damaging area spells
Dismiss the spell as an immediate action when you are caught in someone else's damaging area spell to become immune to that particular casting as well.
With the blood casting class feature you may cast this as a swift action instead of a standard action while bloodraging.

blood-salvation.notes: Dismissible is stated in the prose (dismissing it is how the second, defensive use works).

effects.target: scent
effects.note: only for detecting and pinpointing injured creatures (below full hit points); creatures below half hit points or taking bleed damage count as strong scents

effects.target: Orcs and creatures under the effects of rage gain a +2 morale bonus on attack and damage rolls against creatures they can smell with this spell, or +4 if that creature's blood counts as a strong scent.

blood-scent.notes: The attack/damage bonus is conditional on the recipient being an orc or raging and on the strength of the scent, so emitting a flat combat_mod would apply it to targets that never earn it.

effects.target: An animal sculpture you feed your blood and saliva comes to life and is bonded to you as a familiar, with a familiar's abilities using your caster level as your effective wizard level - but it grants neither the Alertness feat nor its animal type's special ability. If it is slain you take 2 points of Intelligence drain and it becomes a destroyed statue. No effect if you already have a familiar or another blood sentinel.

blood-sentinel.notes: The 2 points of Intelligence drain is a conditional consequence of the sentinel dying, taken by the CASTER, not an effect of casting - deliberately not emitted as an ability_drain spec.

effects.target: Functions as imbue with spell ability, except that only bard spells of the conjuration (healing), enchantment and transmutation schools may be transferred, the imbued spells last 1 day, and the subject is bound by no principles regarding their use. You must shed blood to cast it and cannot cast it at all if you are not susceptible to bleed damage. Each spell imbued costs you 5 hit points that cannot be regained by any means until the spell ends or is discharged.

blood-song.notes: Duration in the corpus is '1 day or until discharged'; emitted as fixed 1 day with the discharge condition named in the narrative, since the shape cannot hold both. The 5 hit points are a casting cost paid per spell imbued, not damage the spell deals.

effects.target: Binds a bound, pinned or helpless hostage within your reach to a member of its family. If neither saves, the relative also takes any damage dealt to the hostage while both live, up to 10 points per caster level per day; this transferred damage is typeless and ignores the relative's DR and resistances. If either target saves you may never exploit the connection between those two creatures again. Each target gains +2 on its save if the two are distant relations or related by marriage, and takes -2 if they are parent and child or siblings.

blood-ties.notes: The damage is transferred from one creature to another rather than dealt by the spell - no damage spec, since a damage spec would have the spell itself harm the target.

effects.target: By consuming 1 pint of blood from a spellcaster killed within the last 24 hours you learn one spell that caster knew, which must also be on your own spell list. You know it for 24 hours, during which you may write it down (or teach it to a witch's familiar) using the normal rules for copying a spell from another source, and prepare it normally.

blood-transcription.notes: Knowledge transfer; nothing in the vocabulary expresses learning a spell.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target bleeds for 1d6 points of damage at the beginning of each of its turns for as long as your own bleed continues. The bleed ends on any target that receives magical healing, and on all of them if your own bleed ends for any reason.

effects.target: Casting cost: you cut yourself with the dagger for 1d6 points of bleed damage to yourself. The spell has no effect at all if you are immune to bleed damage or can reduce or ignore your own bleed.

bloodbath.notes: Two reasons this is not a bleed spec: the amount is dice (bleed takes an integer only), and the damage repeats at the start of every target's turn, which the vocabulary cannot schedule. The caster's own 1d6 bleed is a self-cost with a different recipient from the spell's targets.

effects.target: scent
effects.note: includes the ability to track by scent

effects.target: Perception checks involving smell
Survival checks to track using scent
saving throws against odour-related effects such as the stench ability and stinking cloud
Detect poison by scent with a DC 20 Perception check.

bloodhound.notes: The +8 and +4 are situational_mod rather than skill_mod on purpose: they apply only to smell-based Perception and to scent-based tracking, and a blanket skill_mod would hand the character +8 on every Perception check. The -4 penalty has no stated bonus type, so untyped.

effects.target: When exposed to a mind-affecting effect or a spell that would give another creature control of your actions, dispel this spell as an immediate action to redirect that effect to a creature within 30 feet. That creature saves against the triggering effect's original DC and, on a failure, suffers it - with you treated as the caster, though caster-level-dependent statistics stay those of the original caster. It applies its own spell resistance and immunities normally.
You can have only one instance of this spell active at a time.

bloodstone-mirror.notes: Redirection of an arbitrary triggering effect - no spec type can express 'apply someone else's spell to a new target'.

effects.target: You cut yourself and swear an oath on your own blood, choosing how much damage to take, up to 25 points. That damage cannot be healed while the spell lasts. On any attack, save or check directly related to the oath that brings you closer to fulfilling it, you gain a morale bonus equal to the hit points you took divided by 5; the GM arbitrates what qualifies. The spell ends when you fulfil or forsake the oath, and the lost hit points can then be healed normally.

bloodsworn-retribution.notes: The bonus size is chosen by the caster at casting (damage/5), so there is no number to emit. The '+4' and '20 hit points' in the prose belong to the worked example about Stigur and the bandit leader - not converted. Corpus duration is 'special (see text)'; until_discharged is the only kind that matches 'ends when the oath is fulfilled or forsaken'.

effects.target: Whenever the target hits a creature with a ranged weapon dealing piercing or slashing damage, the creature struck takes 1 point of bleed damage. Unlike most bleed this is cumulative, up to one-half your caster level, to a maximum of 5 points of bleed at 10th level.

bloody-arrows.notes: The bleed is taken by whoever the SUBJECT shoots, not by the subject the spell is cast on. A bleed spec would put it on the wrong creature.

effects.target: The target's natural attacks that deal slashing or piercing damage also inflict bleed damage equal to one-half your caster level, limited by the creature's maximum damage with that attack. This bleed does not stack; when two or more attacks would cause it, take the worse effect.

bloody-claws.notes: Damage from a natural attack, taken by whatever the subject claws - not the spell's own damage and not taken by the spell's target.

effects.target: intimidate
the save DC of your spells with the fear descriptor

Your eyes blacken and weep blood and your teeth become fangs, granting a bite attack that deals 1d3 damage if you are Small or 1d4 if you are Medium. You perceive creatures as though using deathwatch.

bloody-tears-and-jagged-smile.notes: The 1d3/1d4 belongs to a natural attack the spell grants, so it is not emitted as spell damage. Deathwatch perception has no entry in the sense vocabulary.

effects.target: Every kind of writing and recognisable symbol on any surface in a 10-foot-radius burst is smeared illegible - books, stone carvings, even tattoos. It does not touch writing that is not on a surface, such as an illusion, projection or reflection, and has no effect on artifacts. Spellbooks and magic items containing writing, such as scrolls, get a Will save. Against magical writing created by spell effects such as glyph of warding or symbol, blot instead works as dispel magic targeting all such effects in the area.

blot.notes: Alteration of objects plus a conditional dispel; neither is in the vocabulary.

effects.target: The subject's outline blurs and wavers, granting concealment - a 20% miss chance. See invisibility does not counteract it; true seeing does. Opponents who cannot see the subject at all ignore the effect.

blur.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: concealment and percentage miss chance have no spec type and no condition. combat_target has no miss-chance entry, so a 20% miss chance cannot be expressed as a modifier either.

effects.target: As blur, except the concealment (20% miss chance) exists only while you move at least 10 feet on your turn and ends when your movement does - chiefly useful against attacks of opportunity. If you move at least twice your speed on your turn, it lasts until the start of your next turn.

blurred-movement.notes: Same concealment gap as blur, made worse by being conditional on movement within the round.

effects.target: Electricity damage you take while this is active is stored on your skin as though you were holding the charge on a touch spell. Release it with a melee touch attack that deals electricity damage equal to half the largest amount of electricity damage you have taken since casting. Hitting with that touch attack discharges the spell.
the melee touch attack that discharges this spell, when the opponent wears metal armour, carries a metal weapon, or is made of metal

body-capacitance.notes: The damage depends on electricity you happen to have taken, so there is no number to emit; the '15 points' and '7 points' in the prose are a worked example about surviving a lightning bolt. The +3 has no stated bonus type, so untyped. Corpus duration adds 'or until discharged', named in the permission text. Element electricity is already derived from the descriptor.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The primary target's appearance, scent, sounds and mannerisms change to match the secondary target's. While the two are of the same size category they are indistinguishable, so if they stand adjacent any action that would affect one of them - an attack, a targeted spell, an area effect - has a 50% chance of affecting the other instead. Actions that would affect both affect both normally.

effects.target: The disguise does not deceive creatures with true seeing, nor any creature that cannot perceive one of the two targets, even if that creature was fooled earlier; its attacks and targeted spells then resolve normally.

body-double.notes: Illusory identity swap and a 50% redirection chance; neither has a spec type.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target's blood boils, dealing it 1 point of fire damage every round for the duration.

effects.target: No effect on creatures without blood. A target with the orc subtype takes no fire damage and instead gains a +2 morale bonus to Strength.

boiling-blood.notes: 1 point of fire damage PER ROUND - the vocabulary has no repeating-damage type, so this is narrated rather than emitted as a one-shot 1 point of fire. The orc clause is gated on a creature subtype and inverts the effect from harm to a buff, so a flat ability_mod would hand +2 Strength to every non-orc target. Corpus duration is 'concentration + rounds/level'; emitted as the rounds/level tail, since the shape cannot hold both.

effects.target: Fire one ray per round for the duration of the spell, each targeting one living creature.

on_failure.target: dazed

bolts-of-bedevilment.notes: The rounds/level duration is how long you may keep firing rays; each daze lasts 1d3 rounds, carried in the condition's note because a spec's duration field takes no dice.

effects.target: attack rolls made with thrown weapons
The range of any thrown weapon you use increases by 10 feet.

bomber-s-eye.notes: The +1 insight applies only to thrown weapons, so situational_mod rather than a blanket combat_mod on attack.

damage rolls with natural weapons
You are treated as having armor spikes and are proficient with them.

bone-fists.notes: The damage bonus names no bonus type, so untyped, and it applies only to natural weapons, so situational_mod.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.note: living target only; plus 1d6 per 2 caster levels

on_success.note: half damage on a successful save, and the forced movement is negated

effects.target: On a failed save you may also move a living target 5 feet, which does not provoke attacks of opportunity. An undead target with a skeleton takes no damage; instead it must immediately either move up to its speed (provoking normally) or make one attack against a creature of your choice within its reach - the most basic version of that action, activating no special abilities such as grab. A successful save negates this; a mindless undead gets no save.

boneshaker.notes: Damage type is untyped because the prose names none - the harm is a skeleton rattling inside flesh. No cap_dice: the prose states no maximum. The undead branch deals no damage at all and is narrated.

effects.target: water and other liquids such as alcohol and oil
Functions as protection from energy on an object of up to 10 pounds per level, but protects only against acid and fire damage.

book-ward.notes: Refused to emit a resistance spec: this spell inherits protection from energy's absorption pool without restating any number, and the pool size (points absorbed per caster level and its cap) is nowhere in this description. Guessing it would be inventing a number. Corpus duration adds 'or until discharged' - discharge is the moment the borrowed pool runs out.

effects.target: Touch a creature that has at least one manifestation from a corruption and you temporarily gain the stains and gifts that corruption grants it, while the creature keeps them too; gifts with limited uses count as having no uses left for you. Casting costs you 1d3 points of Wisdom drain. In a campaign using the sanity system your sanity score drops by 2 instead (and your sanity edge by 1) - removable only by greater restoration, which clears one such decrease, or by miracle or wish, which clear them all.

borrow-corruption.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the 1d3 Wisdom drain is taken by the CASTER while the spell's target is the creature touched, and no spec has a recipient field. An ability_drain spec would drain the creature you touched - exactly backwards.

effects.target: Cast this immediately upon making a d20 roll, before success or failure is known, to reroll that die and keep the more favourable result.
For the two rounds after casting, you must roll two dice for every d20 roll called for and keep the less favourable result.

borrow-fortune.notes: Corpus duration is 'instantaneous (see text)'; the 'see text' is the two-round penalty, named in the narrative. Reroll mechanics have no spec type.

effects.target: Make a single check with one skill the creature you touched knows, using that creature's skill ranks modified by your own key ability. If the check takes longer than the spell's duration or requires more time, it fails and you must fall back on your own ranks. If the borrowed skill is a class skill for you, you gain the usual +3 class-skill bonus on that check.

borrow-skill.notes: The skill is chosen at cast time from the subject's own ranks, so no skill_mod with a fixed target or amount is possible. The +3 is the standard class-skill bonus, conditional on the borrowed skill being a class skill for you - not emitted as a skill_mod.

effects.target: You gain an extra swift action each turn, usable only on your turn. It cannot be spent on a second immediate action between turns, but it can be spent on a swift action the turn after you took an immediate action.

Each extra swift action costs you 1 point of Constitution damage, or 5 points of hit point damage instead if you are immune to ability damage. When the spell ends the temporal backlash leaves you staggered for 1d4+1 rounds.

borrowed-time.notes: The Constitution damage is a per-use cost, not something the spell deals on casting, and the staggered condition arrives when the spell ENDS - applying it at cast time would stagger the caster for the whole duration. Both narrated.

effects.target: When you throw your next bomb during this extract's duration, choose one target that the bomb's splash damage would normally hit; that target is instead affected as though it took a direct hit.
The change to your magical reserve does not affect discoveries you use to modify bombs. Only one 'bomb admixture' formula can be active at a time - drinking another ends the previous one.

bouncing-bomb-admixture.notes: Modifies how the alchemist's own bomb resolves; the damage is the bomb's, not this extract's.

effects.target: escape artist
grapple combat maneuver checks
CMD against combat maneuver checks to grapple

The target's flesh turns rubbery: it treats any fall as 20 feet shorter (minimum 0) when working out falling damage, and if it falls against a hard surface it may attempt an Acrobatics check (DC equal to the distance fallen) to bounce upward half the distance fallen.

bouncy-body.notes: The Escape Artist bonus is emitted unrestricted because the prose states it unrestricted, even though the two clauses around it are grapple-specific - reading a grapple restriction into it would be adding a rule the text does not have. The grapple CMB and CMD bonuses are situational because combat_target's cmb and cmd cover all maneuvers, not just grapple.

effects.target: Conjures a feast for two creatures per level - hors d'oeuvres, four courses, plentiful drink, on serving trays and in tureens, with place settings, utensils, tablecloths and linens for every diner, adapting itself onto existing tables. No furniture is created. You may specify the type of dish for each course and the beverages; the rest suits the kind of spellcaster you are. The feast and finery vanish after 1 hour, but creatures that partake stay nourished and sated for 24 hours.

bountiful-banquet.notes: Creation; the 24 hours of nourishment outlasts the spell and is named in the text rather than emitted as a second duration.

effects.target: Spend a swift action to direct the bow spirit to fire an arrow or bolt at a target of your choice, as though it were firing the necessary ranged weapon. It uses your base attack bonus plus your Dexterity modifier, along with any feats affecting ranged attacks and any bonuses from the ammunition used, and its attacks do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

The bow spirit is a shapeless force occupying your space and moving with you, drawing ammunition from your quiver and expending it as though you had used it; there must be ammunition available. It cannot be attacked or harmed by physical attacks, but dispel magic, disintegrate, a sphere of annihilation or a rod of cancellation affects it. Its AC against touch attacks is 10 + your Dexterity modifier.

bow-spirit.notes: The attacks are the spirit's, using your own numbers - the spell states no damage of its own.

effects.target: The touched bow becomes as rigid as forged steel and can be wielded as a melee weapon: a shortbow as a club, a longbow as a quarterstaff. It keeps its normal hit points and hardness. Its enhancement bonus, if any, applies on melee attack and damage rolls, and any other weapon special qualities apply to melee attacks too if they can be added to a melee weapon.

bowstaff.notes: The enhancement bonus carried over is the bow's own, an unknown quantity - no combat_mod emitted, since there is no number in the description.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: An indelible rune or mark of no more than 6 characters is etched onto any exposed part of the creature, typically the head or forearm. It can be hidden under clothing, or scraped away at a cost of 1d6 points of damage - but it returns if that damage is healed.

brand.notes: The 1 point of damage is taken by the target on casting, so it is real. The 1d6 is taken later by whoever scrapes the brand off - a consequence of removing it, not of the spell, so deliberately not emitted. Damage type untyped: the prose names none.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target object, Medium or smaller, gains the broken condition. If it was already broken, it is destroyed instead.

break.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: 'broken' is an object condition and is not in the condition vocabulary, which holds only creature conditions. No object hit points or hardness numbers are stated, so nothing else could be emitted.

effects.target: Frees up to one creature per level, all within 30 feet of each other, from enchantments, transmutations and curses - even instantaneous ones. For each such effect make a caster level check (1d20 + caster level, maximum +15) against DC 11 + the effect's caster level; success frees the creature. Against a cursed magic item the DC is the curse's own DC. If the effect is one that dispel magic or stone to flesh cannot undo, this works only if that spell was 5th level or lower. Against a permanent magic item it does not remove the item's curse, but it does free the victim from the item's effects.

break-enchantment.notes: An opposed caster level check against an arbitrary existing effect; remove_condition cannot express it, because what is removed is a spell, not a condition from the vocabulary.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: Each Medium or smaller object in a 30-foot burst centred on you gains the broken condition; an object already broken is destroyed instead. Magic items can be broken this way but not destroyed. Objects in your own possession are not immune.

break-greater.notes: Same 'broken' gap as break. Note the corpus records save as 'none' while the description plainly gives each object a Fortitude save - the description is the authority here, so the save_gate uses Fortitude.

effects.target: saves against very hot conditions, severe heat, breath weapons, and cloud vapours and gases such as cloudkill, stinking cloud and inhaled poisons

A light wind blows against the target from a direction of your choice. The spell does not function without air or underwater. Only one breeze can be active at a time; casting it again dispels the previous casting.

breeze.notes: No bonus type stated, so untyped. The bonus is not on a whole save category - it is on a named list of situations - so situational_mod rather than three save_mods.

effects.target: Once during the duration, as a swift action, will the light to try to end a magical darkness effect within 60 feet of it: attempt a dispel check (1d20 + your caster level) against DC 11 + the darkness effect's caster level. On a success the darkness ends. Either way, this spell's light then dims to the brightness of a torch for the rest of its duration.
Functions as daylight on the object touched, except that it lasts longer.

brightest-light.notes: Inherits daylight's illumination without restating its radius, so no number to emit for the light itself.

effects.target: low_light

A creature that already had low-light vision instead has it enhanced, seeing four times as far in dim light. Creatures within 10 feet of anyone under this spell do not gain concealment from dim light.

brightest-night.notes: The 'four times as far' enhancement has no representation - sense takes a range in feet, not a multiplier on an existing sense.

effects.target: A link between your mind and the subject's feeds it advice for the duration. Each time the subject makes an attack roll, ability check or skill check it rolls two d20s and takes the better result. The spell ends the moment any of those rolls is a natural 20 - your advice is spent.

brilliant-inspiration.notes: Advantage-style rerolling has no spec type. Corpus duration is 'rounds/level and special (see text)'; the 'special' is the natural-20 discharge, named in the text.

effects.target: Each round, as a swift action at the start of its turn, the creature may reduce some or all of its natural armor bonus to AC and gain an equal enhancement bonus on all damage rolls with natural attacks. The trade cannot exceed 1 point per 3 caster levels, to a maximum of -5 AC for +5 damage at 15th level, and natural armor cannot be reduced below 0. The adjusted AC applies against all attacks until the start of its next turn, when it may choose again. No thought is required, so even a creature with no Intelligence score benefits - such creatures always take the maximum reduction and bonus regardless of tactics.

bristle.notes: The amounts are chosen by the creature anew every round and are bounded by its own natural armor, so there is no fixed number to emit; a combat_mod would freeze one of the many legal trades into the only one.

effects.target: Centred on a flat surface you choose, this reduces the hardness of any nonmagical surface in a 5-foot-radius spread by 2 per caster level for the duration.

brittle-portal.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: object hardness has no spec type. damage_reduction is a creature's DR and would be the wrong statistic on the wrong kind of thing.

effects.target: When the imbued slashing melee weapon hits a living creature, its wielder may discharge this spell as a free action to open a gash on that creature's forehead.

The gash deals bleed damage equal to half your caster level. At the start of each of the bleeding creature's turns, when it takes that bleed damage, it also takes a cumulative -1 penalty on all attack rolls. At -3 it treats all targets as having concealment (20% miss chance); at -5 it is blinded. Stopping the bleed ends every effect this spell imposes. A creature immune to bleed damage is immune to all of it.

brow-gasher.notes: The bleed lands on whoever the WIELDER strikes, not on the weapon or its wielder, who is the spell's actual target - a bleed spec here would injure the wrong creature. The escalating penalty and blindness are also gated on rounds of accumulated bleed, which the vocabulary cannot schedule.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: your own Charisma checks and Charisma-based skill checks when interacting with the target

When you fail a Charisma check or Charisma-based skill check while interacting with the target, reroll it as an immediate action. Attempting the reroll grants the target a new saving throw to end the spell.

effects.target: The target does not become hostile when the spell ends, only disillusioned of its new trust. Attacking it or taking any obvious hostile action against it ends the spell at once. Under the contacts rules your trust score with it rises by 1 for the duration; under the individual influence system, a failed initial save also teaches you one of its influence skills, strengths or weaknesses as though you had made a discovery check.

build-trust.notes: The bonus is gained by the CASTER, not by the spell's target, and only while interacting with that target - written into the situational_mod's own text since no spec has a recipient field.

effects.target: str

bull-s-strength-mass.notes: The +4 enhancement is not guessed - it is read from bull's strength's own description in this same corpus, which this spell says it functions like: 'The spell grants a +4 enhancement bonus to Strength'. The only stated difference is that it affects one creature per level.

effects.target: AC against firearm and ranged attacks, including attacks from firearms with the scatter quality
effects.note: +1 more for every five caster levels, to a maximum of +8 at 20th level

bullet-shield.notes: Situational rather than combat_mod on ac because it applies only against firearm and ranged attacks. No scaling block emitted: the progression is +1 per five caster levels on a flat bonus, and the scaling shape's bonus_per_level has no per-levels divisor, so writing one would misstate the rate. The rate and cap are in the note instead.

effects.target: When an opponent shoots at you with a firearm, designate one hovering bullet as an immediate action to block the attack, increasing your AC against that attack by 10. That bullet is destroyed whether or not the attack hits.

Adamantine bullets equal to half your caster level, maximum 4, hover protectively around you. Each has AC 24, 20 hit points and hardness 20. The spell is discharged when every one of them has been destroyed or taken from you.

bullet-ward.notes: The +10 applies to one designated attack at the cost of a bullet, so it is a permission rather than a standing combat_mod on AC.

effects.target: will

effects.target: As a standard action while this lasts, direct your burning gaze at a single creature or object within 30 feet. A targeted creature must succeed at a Fortitude save or take 1d6 points of fire damage; unattended objects get no save.

Like a wall of force it resists dispel magic, though mage's disjunction still works and disintegrate destroys it automatically; contact with a sphere of annihilation or a rod of cancellation destroys it instantly. Weapons and supernatural abilities can damage it: hardness 20, hit points equal to 20 per alchemist level. calamitous-flailing.notes: Same miss-chance gap as blur, compounded by redirection: there is no spec for a percentage miss chance and none for retargeting an attack.

effects.target: Roll 3d8 and consult the Eight Basic Energies table, assigning each die to one of three results. Magic School: you cast all spells of the matching school at +1 caster level. d20 Roll Type: you gain a +2 luck bonus on the matching d20 roll. The foresight is bought with the vulnerability.

calculated-luck.notes: Every one of the three results is determined by a die roll against an external table at cast time - which energy, which school, which roll type. No vulnerability, combat_mod or situational_mod can be written without picking one of eight outcomes and calling it the spell.

effects.target: Summons a wasp swarm (Bestiary 275) that spends the casting time building a 10-foot-by-10-foot nest where you designate, typically under eaves or among rafters. Disrupt the swarm before you finish casting - by attacking it, for instance - and the wasps vanish and the spell fizzles. Once the nest is built the spell also wards the area as alarm: when intruders who do not speak the password come within 20 feet, the swarm leaves the nest and attacks the nearest one, pursuing as best it can, and you have no control over its target or direction thereafter. If the wasps have not left the nest when the spell ends, they and the nest disappear.

calistria-s-guardian-wasps.notes: Summoning plus a ward; the swarm's attacks are the swarm's, not the spell's.

effects.target: Calls the nearest wild animal of a type you designate, whose CR must be no greater than your caster level, to seek you out. It travels under its own power, so its arrival time depends on how near one was; if none can reach you within the duration you become aware of that and the spell is wasted. The GM may allow a DC 15 Knowledge (nature) check to know what animals live in the area. On arrival it comes within 5 feet of you and stays nearby for the duration, starting indifferent and modified by circumstance and interaction. You gain no special influence over it and no ability to communicate with it. When the duration expires it acts according to its attitude - most wander off, though a hungry or provoked predator may attack. Domesticated or trained animals, including familiars and animal companions, are unaffected.

call-animal.notes: Calling and NPC attitude; no spec type covers either.

effects.target: Functions as instant summons, except that it can summon only a construct you control. The specially inscribed sapphire must be worth at least 5,000 gp for constructs immune to magic, such as golems; 1,000 gp suffices for others. If the construct is destroyed or no longer under your control the spell fails, but you learn roughly where it or its remains lie.

call-construct.notes: Teleportation. Corpus duration is 'permanent until discharged'.

effects.target: The first bolt falls the moment the spell completes; each round thereafter you may spend a standard action concentrating on the spell to call another. You need not call one immediately, and may act or even cast between bolts. You may call a total number of bolts equal to your caster level, to a maximum of 10.

Each bolt is a 5-foot-wide, 30-foot-long vertical stroke falling on any target point within range, measured from where you stand at the time; every creature in the target square or in the bolt's path is affected. Outdoors in a stormy area - rain, clouds and wind, hot and cloudy weather, or a tornado, including a whirlwind raised by a djinni or a Large or larger air elemental - each bolt deals 3d10 instead of 3d6. The spell works indoors and underground, but not underwater.

call-lightning.notes: No scaling block: the 3d6 is flat at every caster level - what scales is the NUMBER of bolts, which the scaling shape cannot express. The first bolt genuinely lands on casting, so the damage spec fires at the right moment; later bolts are the permission. Element electricity is already derived.

effects.target: Speak the name of a specific deceased humanoid to call its spirit from its resting place. An unwilling spirit resists with a Will save, modified by how well you knew it - name only +15, secondhand +10, firsthand +5, familiar +0 - and by any physical connection: likeness or picture -2, possession or garment -4, body part or lock of hair or nail clipping -10, different alignment +4. If the chosen spirit resists, another spirit of malevolent intent almost always takes its place to deceive you. A called spirit manifests as a wispy vapour resembling its living form, with the physical attributes of an unseen servant, capable of minor manipulations and of whispering in the languages it knew alive. It is not undead and is not beholden to you; it may refuse to answer or lie using Bluff, and knows nothing of events after its death. Concentrate as a standard action to ask one question per round, up to one question per caster level, each answered the same round. When the spell ends the ectoplasm fades and the soul returns to rest. Spirits of creatures currently undead cannot be called.

call-spirit.notes: A calling with a table of save modifiers; nothing in the vocabulary expresses a save modified by the caster's relationship to the subject.

effects.target: An aura of nothingness channelling the Dark Tapestry surrounds you. Creatures adjacent to you when you cast the spell, and again at the start of each of your turns, take 2d6 points of damage and are fatigued, cannot breathe, and cannot speak or cast spells with somatic components. A Reflex save halves the damage and negates the fatigue, but no save lets an adjacent creature breathe or speak while it remains adjacent to you.

call-the-void.notes: Deliberately not a damage spec. This spell's range is personal and its target is 'you', so 2d6 emitted as an effect would resolve against the CASTER - the damage is taken by whoever stands adjacent. It also repeats at the start of every one of your turns, which the vocabulary cannot schedule. Same reasoning for the fatigued condition.

effects.target: A melee weapon wielded by a willing ally within 30 feet flies telekinetically into your open hand. An unwilling ally makes the spell fail; an unconscious or dying ally counts as willing so long as the weapon is still touching her body.
your own attack rolls and weapon damage rolls with the called weapon, during the round you cast this spell

call-weapon.notes: The bonus is gained by the CASTER while the spell's stated target is the ally's weapon, and it lasts only the rest of that round - both facts are written into the situational_mod's own text because no spec has a recipient field.

effects.target: If your familiar or spirit animal takes hit point damage while within range, it immediately teleports to your space, or adjacent to it, after the damage is applied; if the damage kills it, its corpse teleports instead. callback-greater.notes: The description says only 'as callback, except as noted above', so the body is read from callback's own description in this corpus; the differences are the range and duration lines, which the corpus already carries.

effects.target: Move the calmed area by concentrating as a standard action.

A magical cloud or wind whose point of origin lies inside the area is suppressed entirely; otherwise only the part inside is. Suppression still counts against the suppressed effect's duration. Magical wind and cloud effects are suppressed only if you succeed at a caster level check against DC 11 + the effect's caster level.

calm-air.notes: Weather and environment; wind force is not a statistic the vocabulary knows. suppress_condition takes a creature condition, not a magical area effect.

calm-spirit.notes: Emitted the 1 minute that applies to incorporeal undead; the haunt variant is concentration up to 1 round/level and is named in the text, since the shape holds one duration. Calming a haunt is not a creature condition and has no spec type.

Unsealing or breaking a jar is a standard action that dissipates its power and protection but lets the bearer issue the mummy a short command like a suggestion (Will DC 23 negates). You alone may unseal all 4 jars in a 10-minute ritual to control the mummy as with geas (Will DC 23 negates) - most casters build in a restriction against the mummy harming them, since unsealing the jars leaves them unprotected.

canopic-conversion.notes: Damage type untyped: the descriptors are death and evil, neither of which is a damage type, and the prose names no energy. The damage is taken by the spell's own target at cast time, so it is real.

effects.target: Creates a magical trap on one 5-foot square of stone surface per level, the squares placed anywhere in range and needing not be adjacent, in any mix of stalactites and stalagmites. It triggers whenever a Small or larger creature other than you, your animal companion, familiar or spirit animal moves through an affected square - or at the completion of casting, if a creature already occupies one. Stalactites: shards drop from the ceiling for 3d8 points of bludgeoning and piercing damage (Reflex half) and leave dense rubble that costs 2 squares of movement to enter, adds 5 to Acrobatics DCs and 2 to Stealth DCs; a creature that fails its Reflex save is pinned and entangled until it frees itself with a DC 15 Strength or DC 20 Escape Artist check, and one Small or larger creature can clear the rubble by working for 1 minute. Stalagmites: spires erupt from the ground for 3d8 points of piercing damage and knock the creature prone, with a successful Reflex save halving the damage and avoiding prone; the stalagmites then work as spike stones for 1 minute per caster level before crumbling to dust. effects.target: A 13-hour rite creating one of four ceremonies - funeral, holiday fete, marriage or naming - or one of two ceremonies from your domain, granting a boon to two living, willing, touched subjects for 1 hour per caster level. Only subjects whose alignment is within one step of your deity's can be affected. Bonuses are sacred if you channel positive energy, profane if you channel negative energy. Funeral (requires a corpse and at least one willing companion or next of kin): +2 against death effects. Holiday fete: +1 on Fortitude saves. Marriage (two willing creatures): +1 on saves against fear and emotion effects. Naming (a willing parent and a newborn, who is touched but unaffected): one use of sanctuary. Each domain adds two more ceremonies with their own boons, and each cleric gains the two belonging to her domain.

Augmented ceremonies: under the Ultimate Campaign downtime system you may spend 10 Goods, Labor or Influence, or 2 Magic, to grant an additional boon lasting 1 day per caster level up to 5 days, extending both boons to the creatures touched and to up to your caster level in intelligent, properly aligned creatures within medium range, maximum 10. The augmented version of all four basic ceremonies is the same: a +2 sacred bonus on all saving throws. Use-activated abilities from a boon are supernatural abilities, abilities emulating a spell are spell-like, and both are usable once or until the spell ends, whichever comes first; spell-like abilities use the creature's highest caster level, or CL 1st if it has none. Constant or passive boons can be dispelled as normal against your caster level.

ceremony.notes: Thirty-odd mutually exclusive boons chosen at cast time, each with its own bonus, condition or spell-like ability. Emitting any one of them would make that boon the spell. The base 1 hour/level duration is emitted; the augmented boon's separate 1 day/level (max 5 days) is named in the text. The full boon list stays in the description the corpus already carries, per the brief's instruction not to restate it.

Physical attacks cannot hit or harm it, but dispel magic, disintegrate, a sphere of annihilation or a rod of cancellation affects it normally, and its AC against touch attacks is 10 + your Charisma, Intelligence or Wisdom modifier by class. If it goes beyond the spell's range or out of your sight it returns to you. Against a creature with spell resistance you must make a caster level check the first time the chain succeeds at a maneuver against it; if resisted, the spell is dispelled, and if not, the chain works fully on that creature for the rest of the duration.

effects.target: Metal equipment or 25 pounds of metal per level becomes extremely cold over 7 rounds. Round 1 it is merely cold and deals no damage, and the same is true on round 7. On rounds 2 and 6 it is icy and deals 1d4 points of cold damage; on rounds 3, 4 and 5 it is freezing and deals 2d4. A creature takes full damage if its armor, shield or weapon is affected, and minimum damage (1 or 2 points) if it is wearing or wielding no such item. Unattended nonmagical metal gets no save; magical metal saves, and an item in a creature's possession uses that creature's save bonus unless its own is higher. Any heat intense enough to damage the creature negates this cold damage point for point, and vice versa. Underwater it deals no damage but ice forms around the metal, making it float if unattended. Chill metal counters and dispels heat metal.

chill-metal.notes: The damage is on a per-round schedule that rises and falls (none, 1d4, 2d4, 2d4, 2d4, 1d4, none) and is taken by whoever WEARS the metal, while the spell's targets are the metal items themselves. effects.target: Create an invisible magical sensor at a specific location and hear or see from it - your choice at casting, not both - almost as if you were there. You need no line of sight or line of effect, but the locale must be known to you or else obvious. Once placed the sensor does not move, though you may rotate it in any direction to view the area.

Unlike other scrying spells this one does not let magically or supernaturally enhanced senses work through it. If the chosen locale is magically dark you see nothing; if it is naturally pitch black you see in a 10-foot radius around the centre of the effect. The spell functions only on the plane of existence you currently occupy.

clairaudience-clairvoyance.notes: Scrying. The sense vocabulary covers senses a creature gains in its own body - low-light, darkvision, scent and so on - not a remote sensor placed elsewhere, so this could not go further than a permission.

effects.target: Create a sound like the blast of a mighty horn or trumpet simply by miming the action of sounding one.
